newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end lower but Astra, Skanska gain.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end lower but Astra, Skanska gain.

text.p: Swedish shares ended lower on Friday but negative trends were somewhat counterbalanced by a recovery in drugs major Astra, strong gains for the construction sector and falling bond yields.
The exchange's general index slipped 0.01 percent to 2,638.23 in turnover of 4.53 billion crowns.

"It is a pretty strong bourse considering the downturn in the U.S.," a trader said. "We build our case on the Swedish interest rate fall. If we get an upturn in the U.S. tonight, there is likely to be an upturn here on Monday."
Astra rebounded after falling on Thursday, up five to 356.5.
The construction sector leaped 0.49 percent after Skanska posted strong gains, up seven to 339.

"There is a lot of talk that Skanska, in connection with its 1996 results, will present a restructuring of the company," an analyst said. "The owner Custos has said it will bring out the value in what it owns...and there are some hidden values in Skanska."
The banking sector fell 0.66 percent and Nordbanken kept plummeting on profit taking after surging earlier in the week on merger speculation. The share dropped eight to 263 crowns.
